sources.entry: Screen Loupe - Open-source live magnifier that shows any part of the screen zoomed, pixel-true, in a separate window. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ayenora/screen-loupe) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Screen Loupe
summary.one_liner: A native macOS screen magnifier that mirrors a movable frame over part of the screen into a separate, zoomable, pixel-true viewer window.
use_cases: Check 1px misalignments and antialiasing in a design while editing in Figma or Sketch
Tune front-end layout and see the magnified result next to the code
Build a zoomed picture for a design review or bug report
Simulate colour vision deficiencies to test accessibility
Compare a screen against a design export using Difference blend
summary.what_it_does: Screen Loupe shows a pinned frame over any part of the screen in a separate viewer window, updating live and keeping zoom and framing still while the user keeps working in the underlying app. Zoom goes up to 800% with crisp pixel squares on Retina and non-Retina displays. It includes a Color Meter with HEX, CSS, SwiftUI and AppKit values and a WCAG contrast check, plus rulers, a pixel grid and reference layers with Difference blend. It can simulate six kinds of colour vision and offers copy, snapshot, freeze (F13 or countdown) and split-view tools, along with window snapping and attachment and a screenshot studio with export options.
notable: Open-source core under MIT with official builds adding free closed-source features
Live pixel-true magnification up to 800% with clicks passing through to the app underneath
Colour vision simulation of six types and a Color Meter with WCAG contrast check
No account, no telemetry, and captures stay on the Mac
caveats: Needs Screen Recording access to see the screen
